html:
SMTO-CTX-0053 — SMTO can't find that earlier request in this Code thread

GUID: 4cf8e244-4783-53dd-90f3-97e46a9806be
Slug: code-history-request-not-found
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: code-history

What happened

  • The task tried to reopen an earlier message in this Code thread using a name that doesn't match any finished message it can see. Nothing was run or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task continue. SMTO tells it to search this Code thread for the earlier request. The search returns only finished requests from this thread, each with its correct request ID.
  2. If the task still can't find it, name the file or change you mean in your next message. Each Code message starts fresh, so naming the file gives the task what it needs directly.

What success looks like

  • The task finds the earlier request or continues with the file or change you named.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Code history lookup named a request_id that is not a retained, finished request in the current Code thread.

What this means

  • Code history lookups only return finished requests from the current Code thread, for the same account and workspace. A request_id that was mistyped, belongs to another thread, is still running, or was deleted returns the same response. The lookup runs no command and changes nothing.

Why this can happen

  • The request_id is mistyped, belongs to another Code thread, account or workspace, is still running, or was deleted. All of these return the same response.

How to diagnose it

  • Run read_result(reference='transcript', query=...) in the same Code thread and compare the returned request_id values.

How to fix it

  • Search this Code thread with read_result(reference='transcript', query=...) using words from the earlier request, then read a request_id that the search returned. If no earlier request matches, ask the user which file or change they mean instead of guessing.
  • Search the Code thread transcript with words from the earlier request and use a request_id from the results.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read again only with a different query or a request_id returned by a transcript search.

How to verify the fix

  • A transcript search returns the request_id, or the user names the file or change.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat the same request_id unchanged or guess request IDs.

Technical notes

  • The lookup executes no command and reveals nothing outside the current Code thread.
  • The response does not say which cause applies.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
